cite: Postal Savings & Loan Ass'n v. Powell, 47 S.W.2d 343
court: Court of Civil Appeals of Texas, El Paso
holding_summary: A family occupying part of their own building while renting the remaining rooms to roomers under a 'hotel' sign, with a guest register and meals furnished on request, was held to be conducting a legitimate business sufficient to qualify the property as an exempt business homestead. The court rejected the mortgagee's argument that renting rooms was not a 'calling' or 'business' within the homestead exemption, distinguishing a prior case limiting that holding to its own facts.

quotes.text: The record here shows that the original building occupied by . Powell and Brooks and their wives was a two-story brick veneer ■building containing ten rooms upstairs and about eight downstairs, with the kitchen, and that the families occupied the whole lower floor for living purposes.

The upstairs rooms were rented out to roomers; the building had a sign designating it as the “D. F. Powell I-Io-tel” ; a register was kept; rooms were rented to any one desiring them by the day, week, or longer; stationery was kept for the accommodation of guests; and, when notified, meals were prepared for them.
These facts, in our opinion, are sufficient to show that such a business was being conducted on the property as would be exempt under the definition above quoted.

While there is some authority to the contrary, according to the weight of authority, premises which are used by the owner for the purpose of a hotel of lodging house are exempt as his homestead where he also resides there with his family.

notes: duration_of_occupancy left unclear because the facts describe rentals 'by the day, week, or longer' without singling out a disputed occupancy length.
